title: Best Moiswell Dehumidifier (2026): 70 & 145 Pint Reviewed
dek: Moiswell sells big-capacity basement and commercial units straight to online shoppers. Here's what the numbers really mean — and when a better-known name is worth it.
description: Moiswell dehumidifier reviews for 2026: the 70-pint basement unit and the 145-pint commercial model, what their ratings mean and the best alternatives.
intro: A **Moiswell dehumidifier** tends to show up when you search for a big basement or commercial unit online and sort by capacity. The brand sells mainly through Amazon, and its two best-known models are a 70-pint unit aimed at basements and large rooms and a 145-pint commercial machine for crawl spaces, garages and job sites.

Those headline numbers are eye-catching, and that's exactly why they need a closer look. Dehumidifier capacity depends heavily on the test conditions behind it, and a bigger pint figure on one listing doesn't always mean more water removed than a smaller figure on another. Moiswell is also a younger, less-established name than Frigidaire or AlorAir, which matters when you're counting on a pump and compressor to run for years.
Below we explain what each Moiswell model is good for, how to read its ratings against the competition, and which alternatives we'd consider before you buy.
topPicksLead: For a damp basement, the **Moiswell 70 Pint Dehumidifier** is the Moiswell most shoppers should look at first, as long as you compare its rating against today's 50-pint class rather than taking the 70 at face value.

products.name: Moiswell 70 Pint Dehumidifier
pros: Sized for basements and large open rooms
Digital controls with a humidity setting
cons: Capacity rating needs context against DOE-rated units
Smaller brand with a shorter track record
products.whyWeLoveIt: If you want a full-size basement dehumidifier and don't need a famous name on the front, this is the Moiswell to consider. It's built for the same job as the big-brand 50-pint units: holding a damp, below-grade space around 50% through a humid summer.
products.performance: Treat it as a large-basement compressor unit and compare it with DOE-rated 50-pint models rather than assuming it pulls 40% more water. Set the humidistat at 45–50%, connect a hose to a floor drain if you have one, and let it cycle. As with any unit from a newer brand, read the most recent reviews for patterns before buying, and keep the box and receipt through the return window.

products.name: Moiswell 145 Pint Commercial Dehumidifier
pros: Commercial-style capacity for big, wet spaces
Listed with a pump and drain hose
Built for garages, crawl spaces and job sites
cons: 145 is a best-case figure, not an everyday one
Louder and larger than household units
products.whyWeLoveIt: For a wet crawl space, garage, workshop or a dry-out after a leak, a household unit can run for weeks without catching up. This is Moiswell's answer: a commercial-format machine priced well below restoration-brand LGRs.
products.performance: Commercial units are usually rated at warm, very humid conditions, so the 145-pint figure describes a soaked space, not a typical one. That's fine for flood recovery, where the air really is that wet at first. For ongoing humidity control, a household or crawl-space unit is quieter and more efficient. See how it stacks up against established machines in our [best commercial dehumidifier](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/) guide.

Long track record and a large base of owner reviews

products.whyWeLoveIt: If you're weighing the Moiswell 70 for a basement, this is the like-for-like alternative from a brand with years of owner feedback behind it. It adds a built-in pump, so it doesn't need a floor drain.
products.performance: Amazon lists it as a 50-pint unit with a pump and Wi-Fi, with a coverage claim of up to 7,500 square feet; its 120-pint figure is measured at 95°F and 90% humidity, so make sure you compare it with the Moiswell on a like-for-like rating. The pump pushes water to a laundry sink or out a window, and the app lets you check the basement from upstairs. More options from the brand are in our [best hOmeLabs dehumidifier](/best/best-homelabs-dehumidifier/) guide.

products.whyWeLoveIt: Many Moiswell 145 shoppers are really trying to fix a crawl space. A purpose-built crawl-space unit is quieter, more efficient and designed to run year-round in a cramped, cool space.
products.performance: AlorAir rates it at about 55 pints a day under AHAM conditions and lists operation down to roughly 36°F with auto-defrost. Water leaves through a gravity hose, so plan a downhill route to a sump or the outdoors. Our [best crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) guide covers sizing for sealed crawls.

products.performance: AlorAir rates it at 85 pints a day at AHAM conditions and 180 at saturation, covering up to about 2,300 square feet, with a five-year warranty. Its LGR design keeps pulling water as a space dries, which is where conventional commercial units slow down. See the full brand lineup in our [best AlorAir dehumidifier](/best/best-alorair-dehumidifier/) guide.

blocks.text: Moiswell is a direct-to-consumer brand that focuses on the high-capacity end of the market: basement units, crawl-space and garage machines, and commercial-style dehumidifiers with pumps. You'll mostly find it on Amazon rather than in big-box stores, which means you're relying on the listing, the manual and owner reviews rather than a showroom or a long brand history.

That isn't a reason to avoid it. Several brands we now recommend started the same way. It is a reason to read specs carefully, buy from a seller with a clear return policy and register the warranty as soon as the unit arrives.

We don't run a test lab. For brand guides like this one, we compare the manufacturer's listings and manuals for capacity, test conditions, drainage and controls; check ENERGY STAR and DOE data where models appear; search the CPSC recall database; and read owner reviews for recurring failures such as pumps that quit, sensors that read high and units that arrive damaged.

Because Moiswell's catalog is small, we paired its two most-searched models with the established alternatives most shoppers cross-shop, so you can see what the extra money (or the savings) actually buys.

sections.heading: What to look for in a Moiswell dehumidifier

items.label: The test behind the pint rating
items.text: Look for whether a figure is DOE 2019, AHAM or saturation. Only like-for-like numbers are comparable.

items.label: Drainage that matches your space
items.text: A pump if there's no floor drain or the hose must run uphill; gravity drainage if there's a drain below the unit.

items.label: Low-temperature operation
items.text: Basements and crawl spaces run cool. Auto-defrost keeps the coil from icing below the mid-60s.

items.label: Warranty and support
items.text: Read the warranty terms on the listing and in the manual, and register the unit. With a newer brand, support matters more.
sub: Keep the original box through the return window.
Photograph the serial label for warranty claims.

items.label: Right size, not maximum size
items.text: A commercial unit in a finished basement is loud and wasteful. Our [dehumidifier size guide](/guides/dehumidifier-size-guide/) matches capacity to space.

sections.heading: Is the Moiswell 70 pint really 70 pints?

blocks.text: It depends on the conditions it was rated under. Since 2019, household dehumidifiers sold in the U.S. have been rated under the Department of Energy's test at 65°F, which produces smaller numbers than the older, warmer test did. That's why many units once sold as 70-pint models are labeled 50-pint today, with no change in what they actually remove. Commercial units are often rated warmer and wetter still.

blocks.text: When a listing doesn't say which test it used, assume it's one of the warmer ones and compare cautiously. For household-sized units in this range, our [best 70-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-70-pint-dehumidifier/) and [best 100-pint dehumidifier](/best/best-100-pint-dehumidifier/) guides lay out the options.

sections.heading: Moiswell dehumidifier reviews: what to check

blocks.text: Reviews for any newer brand need a careful read. Star averages hide a lot, and early reviews often come from the first weeks of ownership, before a pump or compressor has seen a full season.

items: **Sort by most recent** to see whether quality has changed between production runs.
**Read the three-star reviews** — they're usually the most specific about noise, drainage and sensor accuracy.
**Look for long-term updates** from owners who've run the unit through a full humid season.
**Note how support handled problems.** A replacement shipped quickly is a good sign; silence is not.
**Check the pump complaints separately.** On any brand, the condensate pump is the part most likely to fail first.

blocks.title: How long should it last?
blocks.text: A well-maintained compressor dehumidifier typically lasts several years. Our [how long do dehumidifiers last](/guides/how-long-do-dehumidifiers-last/) guide explains what shortens or extends that.

The **Moiswell 70 Pint** is a reasonable basement dehumidifier if the price is right and you compare its rating fairly, and the **Moiswell 145 Pint** is a budget route to commercial-scale drying for garages, crawl spaces and leak recovery. If you want a longer track record, the **hOmeLabs 50-Pint with Pump and Wi-Fi** is the safer basement pick, the **AlorAir Sentinel HD55** is the better tool for a sealed crawl space, and the **AlorAir Storm LGR Extreme** is the commercial benchmark.

faqs.q: Is Moiswell a good dehumidifier brand?
faqs.a: It's a newer, online-first brand focused on high-capacity units. Its machines can be good value, but it has a shorter track record than Frigidaire, hOmeLabs or AlorAir, so read recent reviews carefully and buy from a seller with an easy return policy.

faqs.q: Is the Moiswell 70 pint dehumidifier really 70 pints?
faqs.a: Only under the conditions it was rated at. Household units have been rated under the cooler DOE 2019 test since 2019, which yields smaller numbers, so compare it with 50-pint DOE-rated models rather than assuming it removes 40% more.

faqs.q: What is the Moiswell 145 pint commercial dehumidifier good for?
faqs.a: Large, very wet spaces: crawl spaces, garages, workshops and drying out after a leak. The 145-pint figure reflects warm, saturated conditions, so expect less in a cooler, drier space.

faqs.q: Do Moiswell dehumidifiers have a pump?
faqs.a: The 145-pint commercial model is listed with a pump and drain hose. For the 70-pint unit, check the specific listing; if it lacks a pump, you'll need a floor drain below it or an external condensate pump.

faqs.q: Moiswell vs. AlorAir: which is better?
faqs.a: AlorAir has a longer track record, publishes AHAM and saturation ratings side by side and backs its units with multi-year warranties. Moiswell usually costs less. For a crawl space you'll rely on for years, AlorAir is the safer bet.

faqs.q: Can I use a Moiswell commercial dehumidifier in a crawl space?
faqs.a: Yes, for drying one out. For year-round control in a sealed crawl space, a low-profile crawl-space unit with auto-defrost is quieter and more efficient.
